A Long Document on Systems Engineering

Paragraph 1 about memory allocation. Systems that handle memory allocation well tend to share a few traits: they measure before they optimize, they expose small tunable knobs instead of giant switches, and they fail loudly when assumptions break. Over the years engineers have collected a body of folklore about memory allocation, and while the folklore is occasionally wrong, it usually encodes a real failure that somebody paid for in production. When designing around memory allocation, prefer boring solutions whose failure modes you can enumerate on a whiteboard. Exotic designs win benchmarks and lose incidents.
